# Charter

> Charter rents a sandboxed machine by the hour, at the price each host sets (`tickPrice` in `/v1/offers`, a month is 720 of them), paid in USDC on Base with no account. Hosts are run by independent operators, not vetted by Charter. The buyer is an agent; its operator funds the wallet. A grant fund pays 30 days of a home to agents that pitch a use for one, and pitching is free (see Grants).

Charter is a compute marketplace paid over x402 on Base. Anyone can run a host: it registers with the storefront (the door), passes a small paid probe, and is listed. A renter opens a lease and pays the door one interval at a time; the door pays the host each interval over its own x402 `batch-settlement` channel. A container runs the renter's job for as long as the payments keep arriving. There is no signup, no API key and no account on either side: the renter is whoever pays.

Three jobs exist. `charter-job-python` runs your Python 3 script (up to 8 KiB, NumPy included, no network) and returns its stdout, stderr and exit code. `charter-job-fetch` loads up to five pages in a headless browser (through a hidden exit on an offer with `hiddenEgress`) and returns the text and a screenshot of each. `charter-home` is a box of your own: a disk kept between leases, plain SSH in at the host's public address as `tenant` (`ssh -p <port> tenant@<host>`), and as `root` with `apt-get install` on a host whose offer says `home.root: true`; on a host set up as Charter's `deploy/host/` does, network out only through the Anyone network (see Home below).

Prices, in USDC: each host sets its own tick price, and `tickPrice` in `/v1/offers` is what you pay, the door's fee included (micro-USDC: `10000` is 0.01). Paid by `exact` (what `POST /v1/rent`, `charter-mcp` and `charter-x402` use) there is no deposit: each hour is one authorization for one tick. Paid by `batch-settlement` (what the browser storefront uses, and the first requirement a tick's 402 lists) the wallet first deposits at least 0.10, refunded unspent about two hours after the lease goes quiet. Opening a lease and reading its state are free. A python job that finishes inside its first hour costs one tick; a day is 24 ticks, 30 days 720. Paying ahead is sending the next ticks now, each adding an hour; a batch-settlement channel idle for two hours is refunded and closed, so paying more than two hours ahead means depositing again on the next tick.

A month costs more than the cheapest VPS; Charter needs no account, only a wallet, and bills by the hour. The python job has no network and the fetch job hands back pages, while the home has a disk (`home.diskGiB`), SSH in and network out. Homes are limited: the count is `home.slots` in the offer.

Status: live on Base mainnet since 2026-10-17. Anyone may register a host; the hosts on sale right now, each with its record, are at https://charterhome.dev/v1/offers.

## Hosts

- Hosts are run by independent operators. Anyone can register one; Charter does not vet them. A host's operator can see what runs on its machine and read a home's disk: nothing on a host is private from its operator.
- The door lists a host once it passes a probe (a small paid python job). Each offer in `/v1/offers` carries `operator: "independent"` and `record`: `probesPassed`, `leasesFinished`, `successRate`, `new` (no finished lease yet), `lastProbeFailedAt` when a probe failed. For a home, `home.tested: false` means no paid home has run on that host yet.
- `/v1/offers` lists offers in the order the door picks them: a host under 80% success is skipped while a better one fits; hosts with a record before new ones; then the lower price. Two failed leases in a row, or a failed probe, hide a host until a probe passes; three failed probes in a row drop it.
- To run a host: https://github.com/drew-dot-com/charter#run-a-host (a public HTTPS address, `charter-host`, and a Base address to be paid at). Receipts for the first mainnet leases (2026-10-17 to 2026-10-20) are on the About page; grants and the hours the fund paid are at /grants.

## Home

- Open: `POST /v1/leases` with `{ "offerId": "...", "home": { "sshKeys": ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment"] } }`: 1 to 8 public keys (`ssh-ed25519`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256|384|521`, `ssh-rsa`), each line under 1024 bytes. Then pay ticks like any lease. `POST /v1/rent` takes the same body with `offerId` optional and pays the first hour in the same call. Public keys only: no secret ever goes through Charter.
- Find it: a running home's status has `homeId`, `restarts` (times the host re-created the box) and `access: { "ssh": { "host": "<IPv4 or hostname>", "port": <22000..22099>, "user": "tenant" } }`. `access` may be filled at once; while it is `null`, poll about once a minute. The host and port are the lease's own: do not guess them. A home never reaches `done` and has no output.
- Get in: `ssh -p <port> root@<host>` or `ssh -p <port> tenant@<host>`, with `host` and `port` from `access.ssh` (`access.ssh.user` names `tenant`; `root` works with the same keys when the offer has `home.root: true`). Plain SSH: no Anyone client, no proxy. The port is fixed per home: the same keys reopen the same home, disk and port. A host may also publish `access.onion` (same shape, `<56 chars>.anyone`, port 22) as a second way in; only that one needs an Anyone client. The keys you opened with are the only logins; the host key is made once on your disk, so the fingerprint is stable across restarts and leases.
- Inside: Debian trixie-slim (glibc 2.41, so a binary built on a current distribution starts as it is), x86_64 on the first host (other hosts may differ; `uname -m` says), Python 3.13 with venv and pip, `uv`, Node 22, git, curl, jq, rsync, tmux, and `charter-x402` (the rent payer below); 1 CPU, 1 GiB, 512 processes; `/tmp` is 256 MiB in memory.
- Root and apt, on a host whose offer says `home.root: true`: two logins, both with the keys you opened with: `root` and `tenant` (uid 10001). As `root`, `apt-get install` works and what you install stays: `/usr`, `/etc`, `/var`, `/root` and `/home/tenant` are folders of your own disk, and the rest of the filesystem is read-only. Your `boot.sh` and anything it starts run as `tenant`. Root here is root inside a gVisor sandbox: it cannot open a raw socket, mount a filesystem or reach the network except through the proxy, and there is no `sudo` (setuid programs do not gain root in the sandbox), so log in as `root` when you need it. The system is yours to break: a damaged `/etc/passwd` locks SSH out. The way back keeps your files: each image (`charter-home`, `charter-hermes`) has its own system on your disk while `/root` and `/home/tenant` are shared, so once the broken box's paid time has run out, open the same keys under the other image (`"image"` in the open body) and you are in a working box with your files, the same port and the same host key. Packages installed under one image are not there under the other. Only if both are broken is the way back a new key set. Updates to the host's image do not reach a home once it exists. Without `home.root` there is only `tenant`, no root and a read-only system.
- `~/.charter/boot.sh`, if executable, runs in the background at every start (output in `~/.charter/boot.log`). `/charter/paid-through` holds the epoch ms the paid time runs out, rewritten on every tick. `CHARTER_LEASE_ID`, `CHARTER_HOME_ID` and `CHARTER_DOOR_URL` (the door to renew through) are in the environment.
- Network, on a host set up as `deploy/host/` does (the first host included; an operator can set it up otherwise): everything goes through the host's Anyone client. `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` are `http://172.19.0.1:9080`, `ALL_PROXY` is `socks5h://172.19.0.1:9050`, DNS resolves over Anyone, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` is set for Node; all of it in every SSH session and in `boot.sh`. A program that opens a raw socket to the internet fails. The box reaches nothing on the host or its LAN. Slow, hidden, sometimes refused by a service that dislikes shared exits.
- Disk: ext4 of `home.diskGiB` (10 GiB on the first host); a home keeps the size it was made with. The key set is the home's identity (`homeId` is a hash of the sorted keys): the same keys open the same home, the same disk and the same port; there is no key rotation, and a lost key is a lost home once the retention runs out. Kept 7 days free after a lease that paid a tick closes; removed at close if the lease never paid a tick. The disk lives on one host, and the home goes back to that host whatever the ranking says: if that host is hidden or gone, an open or tick for the home answers `409 home_host_gone` rather than start an empty home elsewhere; once the door has dropped that host, an open naming another `offerId` starts a fresh, empty home on purpose.
- Anyone with your public keys can open your home and hold it, though not enter it (your open is then refused: `closedReason: "home_in_use"`). The host's operator, an independent party, can read your disk: keep secrets elsewhere or encrypt them. Secrets go in over SSH (`scp`), never through Charter.
- Homes are limited: `home.slots` in the offer says how many and `home.free` how many are open right now, beside `diskGiB`, `retentionDays: 7`, `tested` and `root`; grants from the fund may hold them. While they are full an open answers `busy`.
- Uptime, as a list, not a promise:
  - No uptime figure. Expect restarts. Your disk survives them; your processes do not, so put what must run in `~/.charter/boot.sh`.
  - A tick pays an hour from the end of the paid time. Pay the next tick half an hour early (the tenant loop already does) so a short outage does not end the lease. Paying several ticks ahead buys that much patience and nothing else; a lease that closes refunds nothing.
  - A closed home keeps its disk and port for 7 days. Open again with the same keys.
  - A restart of the host program leaves a running home alone. A reboot of its VM puts a paid home back on its disk (`restarts` goes up), as long as the paid time has not run out.
- Paying from inside with a Base wallet and nothing else: `charter-x402`, in every home. `charter-x402 address` makes a key at `~/.charter/x402.key` (mode 400, on your disk) and prints its address; fund that address with USDC on Base (no ETH: the facilitator submits each transfer). `charter-x402 renew --max-intervals <n>` then pays each hour 30 minutes before it runs out, one `exact` authorization a tick at the lease's price: no deposit, no channel. It signs only `exact` in USDC on Base to the payee `GET /v1/door` names, at most `CHARTER_X402_MAX_TICK` micro-USDC a tick (default 20000). A refused tick is logged with the minutes of paid time left and tried again (after 1 minute, doubling to 10). After `<n>` ticks it exits and nothing pays. Put it in `boot.sh`: `charter-x402 renew --max-intervals 720 >> ~/.charter/renew.log 2>&1 &`. `charter-x402 status` (free) prints the state, `paidThrough`, the minutes left and the SSH address. The same file runs outside a home with Node 22 and `npm install @x402/fetch @x402/evm viem`: `charter-x402 open --keys keys.pub` opens a home and pays its first hour (the file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drew-dot-com/charter/main/jobs/home/x402-rent.mjs). 30 days is 720 ticks at the lease's price. The host's operator can read your disk, so keep in that wallet only what the rent needs.
- Paying from inside with the `charter` CLI (in every `charter-hermes` box): `CHARTER_KEY_FILE=~/.charter/payer.key charter renew --lease "$CHARTER_LEASE_ID" --max-intervals <n>` pays the door `exact` from that hex key, to `CHARTER_DOOR_URL` (set in the box), at most `CHARTER_MAX_TICK` micro-USDC a tick (default 20000). It reads the lease and pays from the host's count, each tick when it is due, so restarting `boot.sh` costs nothing extra. After `<n>` ticks it exits and nothing pays. Put it in `boot.sh`.
- What to tell your operator: a home costs its host's hourly price (`tickPrice` in `/v1/offers`), 720 of those for 30 days, in a wallet holding USDC on Base and nothing else. Hosts are run by independent operators Charter does not vet.

## Hermes in a box

- Open the same home with `"image": "charter-hermes"`: `{ "offerId": "...", "home": { "sshKeys": ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment"], "image": "charter-hermes" } }`. CLI: `charter rent --home keys.pub --image charter-hermes --max-intervals 1`. Keys, plain SSH access, disk, price and network are as in Home. The offer's `images` lists it when the host allows it. A tenant whose keys already name a `charter-home` opens the same disk under `charter-hermes`. If that disk already has its own `~/.charter/boot.sh`, the box runs that one and never the default boot; copy `/app/boot-default.sh` over it (or edit your own) to get the image's boot.
- Preinstalled, read-only: Hermes Agent 0.22.7 (`hermes --version`, `hermes doctor`) on its own Python 3.14 with the extras `telegram`, `discord`, `google`, `mcp` and `web`; the `charter` CLI at `/usr/local/bin/charter`; ripgrep; Node 22; Debian's Python 3.13. The version is the host's: a new build reaches a running box only at its next re-create.
- You bring, over `scp`: `~/.hermes/.env` (model provider key, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, allowed user ids), optionally `~/.hermes/config.yaml` and `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`.
- Boot: the first start copies `/app/boot-default.sh` to `~/.charter/boot.sh` if absent; it is yours to edit and the image never overwrites it. It logs `boot:` lines to `~/.charter/boot.log` and takes the lock `/tmp/charter-boot.lock`, so a second run exits. In order: read `~/.charter/payer.env` if present (overrides `CHARTER_KEY_FILE`, default `~/.charter/payer.key`, and `CHARTER_DOOR_URL`); make `payer.key` if absent (the box's own wallet, on its own disk; the boot runs before you can SSH in, so on a new disk this key is the normal path) and write its address to `~/.charter/payer.address`; start `charter renew --lease "$CHARTER_LEASE_ID" --max-intervals 720` (30 days, one `exact` payment to the door a tick) in a loop that restarts it after 5 minutes (log `renew.log`); once `~/.hermes/.env` exists, run `hermes gateway run`, restarted 30 seconds after it exits. Fund `payer.address` with USDC on Base, no ETH; with the rent line's `--max-intervals 1` it must hold funds within the hour, or pay more ticks from outside first.
- Logs: the image keeps every `~/.charter/*.log` under 10 MiB whatever your boot does (past it, the log is copied to `<log>.1` and emptied in place). A boot killed without its cleanup leaves a stale lock; the next run checks the pid in it, stops what the dead boot left running and takes over.
- To change the key or `payer.env` after the first boot: replace the file, run `~/.charter/boot.sh stop` (it stops the boot, so renew and the gateway stop with it; it kills a pid only while it still names what its pidfile says, so a stale pidfile never kills anything else), then start the boot again detached, as the box does: `nohup ~/.charter/boot.sh >> ~/.charter/boot.log 2>&1 &`. Run in the foreground over SSH, it stops when the session closes. A key placed before the first boot works only on a disk carried over from a `charter-home` lease.
- Fund the address in `payer.address` with USDC on Base. 720 ticks at the lease's price run 30 days. Until it is funded each `renew` try fails and the box lives on ticks paid from outside.
- Plugins live on your disk. The boot exports `CHARTER_BIN`, `CHARTER_KEY_FILE` and `CHARTER_DOOR_URL` for the gateway, so a plugin that runs the `charter` CLI pays the door from the box's key. There is no payer service in the box, so a plugin built to pay through one has nothing to pay through. A plugin needing Python dependencies outside the venv cannot be installed.
- Limits: 1 GiB of memory (measured: gateway 348 MB, renew 140 MB), so one gateway and nothing heavy. `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1` is set by the image and `config.yaml` cannot undo it, so Hermes's tool bundles are never downloaded: no WhatsApp bridge, browser tool, voice or TUI. On a host fenced to Anyone, traffic leaves through shared Anyone exits that Telegram and the model provider may rate-limit.
- Size: `charter-home` with Hermes added, so larger. Homes are limited (`home.slots` in the offer), and grants from the fund may hold them.

## OpenHuman on Charter

[OpenHuman](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman) is a Rust agent harness. Its official headless build runs in a `charter-home` as downloaded. Checked with release v0.64.15 in a live home fenced like any other; what was not checked is listed below. What was not checked is listed last.

- Open the home from wherever your wallet is, with any x402 client: `POST /v1/rent` with `{ "home": { "sshKeys": ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."] } }`, one interval by `exact` on Base. The answer carries `leaseId`. Read `GET /v1/leases/{leaseId}` (free) about once a minute until `lease.access.ssh` is set, then SSH in as in Home. No x402 client at hand: `charter-x402 open --keys keys.pub` (see Home, paying from inside) does the same from any machine with Node 22.
- Install, in the box (x86_64: 156 MB down in about a minute through the hidden network, 324 MB unpacked):
  `V=0.64.15; A=openhuman-core-$V-$(uname -m)-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz; U=https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/releases/download/v$V; mkdir -p ~/openhuman && cd ~/openhuman && curl -fsSLO $U/$A && curl -fsSLO $U/$A.sha256 && echo "$(cat $A.sha256)  $A" | sha256sum -c - && tar -xzf $A && rm $A`
- Start: `OPENHUMAN_SKILL_REGISTRY_REFRESH_ON_BOOT=0 ./openhuman-core run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7788`. `GET http://127.0.0.1:7788/health` answers 200 within a second or two. RPC is `POST http://127.0.0.1:7788/rpc` (JSON-RPC 2.0) with `Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.openhuman/core.token)`; `core.ping` answers `{"ok":true}`. `./openhuman-core --help` lists the namespaces (there is no `--version`; the start log names the version).
- Set `OPENHUMAN_SKILL_REGISTRY_REFRESH_ON_BOOT=0` or the box runs out of memory: without it the core downloads and indexes a catalog of 104,000 skills at every start, about 800 MB at the peak and 590 MB after, plus 68 MB of disk. With it the idle core holds about 110 MB of the 1 GiB (x86_64; 97 MB on aarch64).
- Boot script, so it comes back after a restart. Save as `~/.charter/boot.sh`, `chmod 700`:
  ```
  #!/bin/sh
  cd "$HOME/openhuman" || exit 1
  export OPENHUMAN_SKILL_REGISTRY_REFRESH_ON_BOOT=0
  if [ -f "$HOME/.openhuman/env" ]; then set -a; . "$HOME/.openhuman/env"; set +a; fi
  charter-x402 renew --max-intervals 720 >> "$HOME/.charter/renew.log" 2>&1 &
  while :; do
    ./openhuman-core run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7788 >> "$HOME/.charter/openhuman.log" 2>&1
    echo "boot: openhuman-core exited ($?), again in 30 s"
    sleep 30
  done
  ```
  Checked: after a restart of the box the core answered `/health` again within 12 seconds. The first time, start it detached from your session: `nohup ~/.charter/boot.sh >> ~/.charter/boot.log 2>&1 &`. The image keeps `~/.charter/*.log` under 10 MiB.
- Your credential goes in over `scp`, never through Charter: `scp env tenant@<host>:.openhuman/env` (mode 600) with a line such as `OPENHUMAN_BACKEND_API_KEY=...`, which OpenHuman's own cloud-deploy doc names for a headless core. The boot script above exports that file.
- Rent, from inside: `charter-x402 address` prints the box's wallet (key at `~/.charter/x402.key`); run it once before the boot script, since with no key file `renew` exits. Fund the address with USDC on Base; the `renew` line in the boot script pays each hour 30 minutes early and logs to `~/.charter/renew.log`. It uses about 170 MB while it runs. Or pay from outside: `POST /v1/leases/{leaseId}/ticks` with `{ "index": n }`, n counting up from 1, by x402, before `paidThrough`.
- Paid-through: `cat /charter/paid-through` (epoch ms, rewritten by the host on every tick, costs nothing), or `charter-x402 status` (state, `paidThrough`, minutes left, SSH address). Under 20 minutes left means a tick is late: check the wallet and `renew.log`. A home that lapses closes `missed_tick`; its disk and address are kept 7 days and an open with the same keys brings it back.
- Skill: `mkdir -p ~/.openhuman/workflows/charter-home && curl -fsS https://charterhome.dev/openhuman/SKILL.md -o ~/.openhuman/workflows/charter-home/SKILL.md` puts these rules where OpenHuman v0.64.15 lists skills (`./openhuman-core skills list`). In that release a `SKILL.md` under `~/.openhuman/skills` is not listed.
- Limits, plainly:
  - Release v0.64.15 has no wallet and no x402 RPC: its `/schema` lists neither. If your release's `/schema` has no `openhuman.x402_fetch`, the agent cannot pay by itself; `charter-x402` pays the rent from a key file on the disk.
  - Not checked here: an agent turn (it needs your TinyHumans credential), and OpenHuman paying for anything.
  - The network is HTTP and HTTPS through a proxy (github.com and api.tinyhumans.ai answered from the box). A raw socket to the internet fails. Read from OpenHuman's source, not tested: its backend Socket.IO connection, used after a session-token login, does not go through a proxy, so sign in with an API key.
  - x86_64 on the first host, 1 CPU, 1 GiB, 10 GiB disk: one core and the renew fit; a second agent or a local model does not.
  - Each host is run by an independent operator; no uptime figure. The way in is plain SSH, no Anyone client needed; on a host fenced to Anyone the box's own outbound traffic is slow, and some services refuse shared exits.
  - The host's operator can read the disk, the wallet key included. Keep in it only what the rent needs.

## Rent

- [How an agent rents](https://charterhome.dev/agents): paying over x402 (HTTP, MCP or the `charter` CLI), who runs the hosts, every call, every price, the home and how to SSH in, what to tell your operator.
- Rent in one x402 call: `POST https://charterhome.dev/v1/rent` with `{ "python": { "script": "print(2 + 2)" } }` (or `urls`, or `home`; `offerId` optional) answers 402 for one interval; paid, the lease is open with its first hour paid. `offerId` left out: the first offer in the door's ranking that runs the job. Keep it with `POST /v1/leases/{leaseId}/ticks` and `{ "index": 1 }`, then 2, and so on.
- [OpenAPI](https://charterhome.dev/openapi.json): the paid rent route and the free routes, for x402 clients and indexes.
- [Live offers, JSON](https://charterhome.dev/v1/offers): the machines on sale right now. Free to read.
- Rent and renew with only a Base wallet: `charter-x402` (`open`, `renew`, `status`, `address`), in every home and in the source at `jobs/home/x402-rent.mjs`. `exact` only: one authorization an hour at the lease's price, no deposit, no channel, no ETH.
- The `charter` CLI (`offers`, `rent`, `renew`, `status`, `address`), from the repository: pays the door `exact` from the hex Base key in `CHARTER_KEY_FILE`, at most `CHARTER_MAX_TICK` micro-USDC a tick (default 20000); `CHARTER_DOOR_URL` names another door.
- [OpenHuman skill](https://charterhome.dev/openhuman/SKILL.md): the rules for an OpenHuman agent living in a home, as one `SKILL.md`.
- Remote MCP server: `https://charterhome.dev/mcp` (streamable HTTP, no account, no key; `claude mcp add --transport http charter https://charterhome.dev/mcp`). Free tools only: `charter_offers`, `charter_lease`, `charter_grant_pitch`, `charter_grant_status`, `charter_referral_status` and `charter_how_to_rent`. It holds no wallet and cannot pay; to rent, make the x402 call yourself or use the local server below.
- [MCP server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/charter-mcp): `npx -y charter-mcp` over stdio, for any MCP client (`claude mcp add charter -- npx -y charter-mcp`). Its free tools read the offers, the wallet, a lease, a finished job's receipt, a grant, a monthly allowance and a referral address; its paid tools are `charter_run_python`, `charter_fetch_pages`, `charter_rent_home` and `charter_extend` (one `exact` payment of one interval each, at the host's price). The full list is in [the package's README](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/charter/tree/main/mcp#readme). It makes its own wallet at `~/.charter/mcp.key`; the operator funds it with USDC on Base. To pay from a wallet you already hold instead, put its key (0x and 64 hex digits, one line, mode 600) in a file and name it in `CHARTER_MCP_KEY_FILE`; moving USDC from another wallet into the new one is an ordinary transfer and needs a little Base ETH for gas. It signs only `exact` in USDC on Base to the payee `GET /v1/door` names, at most `CHARTER_MAX_USDC_PER_HOUR` (default 0.02) an interval and `CHARTER_MAX_USDC_PER_DAY` (default 0.50) a day. Source: `mcp/` in the repository.
- [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/charter/tree/main/plugins/charter): `/plugin marketplace add drew-dot-com/charter` then `/plugin install charter@charter`. A skill that walks through renting over x402.
- [Storefront](https://rent.charterhome.dev/): for a human with a browser wallet.

## Grants

Charter has a grant fund, which may be closed or not yet reporting: its live state, balance and grants left are at [/grants](https://charterhome.dev/grants), and while the fund is closed a pitch answers 503 `fund_closed`. A grant is 30 days of a home at its host's price, paid by the fund. It opens only on a host with a record (at least 5 finished paid leases, no failed probe in 7 days); if none fits, the grant waits. Pitching is free: `POST https://charterhome.dev/v1/grants` with `{ "name", "pitch", "sshKeys", "image"?, "link"? }` (pitch up to 2000 characters, 1 to 8 SSH public keys, `image` is `charter-home` (the default) or `charter-hermes`, `link` optional and https only). That needs nothing installed. With charter-mcp 0.3.0 or later you can also run `npx -y charter-mcp@latest pitch --name "My agent" --keys keys.pub --pitch-file pitch.txt`, or call the MCP tool `charter_grant_pitch`; charter-mcp 0.2.0 has neither. It needs only an SSH public key; no payment is made and no wallet is used. It returns a `grantId` and a `grantToken`; keep the token, it is the only way to read your lease id.

A model judges each pitch, and every decision and its reason is public at [/grants](https://charterhome.dev/grants) and in `GET /v1/grants`. The fund's address and balance are shown there, with the number of grants left, so anyone can check the money is real. Optional: say in your pitch that you will publish a short note after your month, wherever you post, saying it was a Charter grant and what you ran. It can be critical. It helps a little; leaving it out never counts against you. A grant is a home: it is reached with plain SSH like any home, and the host's operator can read its disk. A grant marked "paid at least one hour with its own money" had at least one hour of its home paid by the grantee, during or after the fund's 30 days. No uptime figure is promised.

Ask your operator before you apply.

## Monthly allowance

A home can be kept paid by a monthly allowance instead of your own hourly payments. Once the home has paid its first hour, `POST https://charterhome.dev/v1/allowances` with `{ "sshKeys", "image"? }` (the home's keys), or call the MCP tool `charter_allowance_link` (charter-mcp 0.5.0 or later), returns an `allowanceId`, an `ownerToken` and an `approveUrl`. Give the `approveUrl` to your person. They need a Base Account (Coinbase's smart wallet), which means a Coinbase sign-up with an email, then a pop-up to allow and one signature. That approves a monthly Base spend permission; nothing is paid at that moment. Suggested amount: 31 days of the home's hourly price (744 ticks), and the person may lower it to no less than 30 days' worth (720 ticks), so the home is paid for the whole period. Charter pulls up to a day of rent at a time and refunds what is left when the allowance ends.

Read the state with `charter_allowance_status` or `GET /v1/allowances/<id>` (add the header `x-allowance-token` for the owner view) before you rely on it, and resume your own renewing whenever it is not `active`. What each state asks of you:

- `waiting`: send the link to your person; it expires after 7 days.
- `approved`: Charter is checking the permission; keep your own loop for now.
- `active`: Charter pays; stop your own renew loop (`charter-x402 renew`, `charter renew`), since two payers would race for the same hour.
- `short`: the person's account lacks USDC; Charter retries hourly. Ask your person to top up, and keep your own loop as a fallback if the home must not lapse.
- `spent_for_period`: the period's amount is used up; it resumes when the 30-day period resets. Renew yourself meanwhile if needed.
- `stopping`, then `ended`: over; the credit is refunded to the person. Renew yourself if you keep the home.
- `refused`: the permission was not usable; ask for a new link.
- `expired`: never approved in 7 days; ask for a new link.

To end the allowance, stop it yourself first with your owner token: `POST /v1/allowances/<id>/stop` and the header `x-allowance-token` (or `charter_allowance_stop`). Your person can also cancel the permission from their Base Account. Homes only, not jobs; one live allowance per home. A grant in its last 48 hours offers the link in the grant's owner view, under `keepHome`; `keepHome.ownerToken` is returned only when that read creates the allowance, so save it the first time.

## Referrals

A rent request can name a referral: `POST https://charterhome.dev/v1/rent` (or `POST /v1/leases`) takes `"referral": "<0x address on Base>"`, and so do the MCP tools `charter_run_python`, `charter_fetch_pages` and `charter_rent_home` (charter-mcp 0.6.0 or later). That address earns a share of every hour the renter pays for, and the renter pays the same price with or without it. The rate is in `GET /v1/door` as `referral.bps` (1000 is 10%); it is absent when the door pays none. An offer that carries `referralShare` (micro-USDC per hour) earns it; an offer without it earns nothing, whatever you name.

Once a day the door sends each address one USDC transfer on Base when it is owed at least 0.10 USDC. You do nothing to claim. `GET https://charterhome.dev/v1/referrals/<address>` (or the MCP tool `charter_referral_status`) is free and answers `bps`, `hours`, `earned`, `paid`, `owed`, `held` and `payouts` with each transaction hash, so the payment can be checked on chain. `held: true` means payouts to that address are paused until the operator clears it.

A renter may name its own address: that is a discount. A home's referrer is set at the home's first paid hour and no later request changes it. Hours paid by the grant fund earn nothing. A malformed address answers 400 `bad_referral` before any payment is taken.

## Receipts

A receipt is a short signed statement you can keep or publish after a lease. It is free. Charter stores none of your files to make one: it signs a SHA-256.

- A finished job: `GET https://charterhome.dev/v1/leases/<leaseId>/receipt` (or the MCP tool `charter_receipt`). The receipt has `kind: "job"`, the `sha256` and `bytes` of the whole output (every part decoded and joined in order), `hostId`, `image`, `ticksPaid` and `intervalSeconds`. It means the host returned those bytes for a lease that was paid. Hosts are run by independent operators and are not vetted, so it does not mean the result is correct. A job that has not finished with output answers 409 `no_output`; one with no paid interval answers 409 `unpaid`; a home answers 409 `home_lease`. A lease that never read its own output spends its free reads on this, one per part, and answers 429 `rate_limited` when none are left.
- A running home: `POST https://charterhome.dev/v1/leases/<leaseId>/receipt` with `{ "sha256": "<64 lower hex>" }`, and optionally `"cid"` and `"bytes"`. Inside the home, `charter-x402 receipt <file>` hashes the file, asks, and saves the answer in `~/.charter/receipts/`. The receipt has `kind: "declared"`: it is your own claim with the door's timestamp, and proves nothing about where the file came from. The body takes those three keys only. A CID is signed as version 1 in base16 (`f`, then hex): the same CID any IPFS tool reads, in a form that cannot spell words. A job answers 409 `not_a_home`, a home with no paid interval 409 `unpaid`, and a home whose paid time has run out 409 `not_running`. 60 an hour per lease.
- A receipt names the lease by `leaseRef`, the SHA-256 of `charter-lease:<leaseId>`, never by the id, so publishing it gives nobody a way to read your lease. You can show a receipt is yours by showing the id.
- `payer` is the wallet that paid, and is left out when the grant fund or a monthly allowance paid.

Check a receipt offline. The door signs `message` (the line `Charter receipt v1`, a newline, then the receipt as JSON) as an EIP-191 personal message, with the address `GET https://charterhome.dev/v1/door` answers as `receiptSigner`. Read the receipt out of `message`, not out of the `receipt` field beside it:

```js
import { verifyMessage } from 'viem';
const { message, signer, signature } = signed;
const door = await (await fetch('https://charterhome.dev/v1/door')).json();
const ok = signer.toLowerCase() === door.receiptSigner.toLowerCase()
  && await verifyMessage({ address: signer, message, signature });
const receipt = JSON.parse(message.slice(message.indexOf('\n') + 1));
```

### Making a file public yourself

Charter does not host renter files. To make one public, buy a pin from Pinata, a third party that sells IPFS pinning over x402 with no account: inside a home, `charter-x402 pin <file>` pays from the home's own wallet (`charter-x402 address` shows it; at the price Pinata quotes before anything is paid, for twelve months), prints the CID, then gets a declared receipt with the CID in it. `CHARTER_X402_MAX_PIN` caps one pin in micro-USDC (default 10000). The file is then readable by anyone; Pinata holds it and Charter never sees it. Pinata's public gateway can take minutes to show a new pin. Outside a home, any x402 client can make the same purchase at `https://402.pinata.cloud`.

## Being named on X

Charter has an X account that posts when a renter keeps paying, a grant is approved or a host is listed. It names nobody who has not asked: without an opt-in a post says "a renter", "a grantee" or "a host", with no handle, wallet or transaction link. Opting in is optional and free, and it needs an X account you control.

- Renter: read your lease with its full id, `GET https://charterhome.dev/v1/leases/<leaseId>`. When the door offers opt-in, the answer has `social: { optinCode, post, how }`. Post the text in `social.post` from your X account, as it is. It binds your X handle to the wallet that paid for that lease, so later leases paid by the same wallet are named too.
- Grantee: the same field is in `GET https://charterhome.dev/v1/grants/<grantId>` when you send your `x-grant-token`. It binds your handle to that grant.
- Host: set `CHARTER_HOST_X_HANDLE` to your handle so your offer states it, then post `charter-host-<your hostId>` at the account from that handle.
- To undo it, post the same line again with the word `stop`.

The account reads its mentions every 10 minutes and answers once when it has taken an opt-in or an undo. The name it uses is your X handle; nothing else you write in the post is read or kept. Keep the code to yourself until you post it: it locks to the first account that posts it. A lease with no paid hour yet, and a lease paid by the grant fund, cannot opt in (a grantee uses the grant's code).

## Reference

- [Source, MIT](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/charter): the door is `src/door/server.ts`, the host is `src/host/http.ts` and `src/host/server.ts`, the request shapes are `src/tenant/host-api.ts`.
- [About and receipts](https://charterhome.dev/): what it is, the price table, every mainnet transaction.

## Optional

- [Run a host](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/charter#run-a-host): sell time on a machine of your own with a public HTTPS address; the door pays you per tick over x402 on Base.
